reviews.text: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44181848/] 【更多适合Steam Deck的好游戏推荐，请关注GPD掌机鉴赏家！】[/url] 《禁忌星域》这款游戏，最初吸引我的机甲割草的新鲜感（虽然大屁股也非常吸引我）。游戏的美术和设定有其亮点，角色立绘风格鲜明，带有动态效果，场景也试图营造出克苏鲁式的诡异氛围。其核心玩法是经典的类幸存者模式，武器组合和局外基地养成系统提供了一定的构筑深度和重复可玩性。 然而，当前市面上同类玩法游戏已经非常多了。正式版将宣传重点和实际体验都放在了“美少女”元素上，但相关的互动内容深度有限，如果玩家对此不特别感冒，那么游戏在玩法上提供的独特竞争力就显得有些薄弱。加上目前版本还存在一些优化问题，后期弹幕一多容易卡顿，进一步影响了割草的爽快感。 像我一样对“美少女+幸存者”这个组合有特别的偏爱，值得一玩。但如果更期待的是那种侧重机甲对抗的硬核体验，或者寻求玩法上有重大突破的幸存者游戏，那么可能需要谨慎考虑。
越更新bug越多，现在经验和晶核捡不了

游戏有热水器可以是好添头，总有人看见奈子就走不动道，但是游戏不能只有热水器。 游戏方面吸血鬼like的下限就摆在那儿了，不可能做得很烂，好歹玩的下去，但是细节方面最让人头疼的是游戏后期满屏的小怪和各种花里胡哨的爆炸特效，以至于你在快乐拆罐子的时候突然撞在了直接穿墙过来的小怪上，而且你装怪收到伤害的CD极短，一眨眼就能从满状态掉到三分之一乃至更低，然后你心一慌，去找血罐&等自然回血，路上一堆特效让你根本看不清有没有漏网的小怪朝你走过来，一个不注意，恭喜你，打了半天的局直接灰屏失败了。 局外养成方面和角色我真的想问一句何意味啊，我打了快九个钟头能够走线性流程获得的角色就两个，一个是初始角色，另外一个是成就里建建筑送的，我一开始还纳闷呢，合着是让我买DLC拿吗，一看建筑差点没给我气笑，一个猛猛烧灵魂碎片的建筑，我现在升到十级，运行三十几分钟判定一次，还是有概率获得角色。这时候我一下子释然了，为什么我来打个单机游戏我还要抽卡来获得角色啊，搞这些有的没的来强行拉长游戏流程......转念一想，我应该换位思考，作者千辛万苦做出来的游戏肯定希望我们好好体验，那我也应该尊重一下，大不了自适应一下改个数据呗，于是乎打开CE准备改一下灵魂碎片体验一下这个抽卡（对，我玩了八个多钟头产出都不够我判定一次的），结果里面资源的数量在停止生产之后会把小数点后面的给抹掉，这就直接导致CE很难直接去修改数值......行，那我还是不玩了，所以愤愤地出来写了这篇测评。 美术方面，2D立绘确实是大大大，相信很多hxd跟我一样就是冲着大奈来的，但是我想给各位泼一盆冷水，这部游戏的美术高光基本上就止步于2D立绘和动态表现了。局内只有左下角一个角色立绘，除此以外几个角色根本没有区别，战甲的建模在不同角色身上全是一样的，而且粗糙得有点不好评价了，之前看预告局内操纵的还是机械兽，那3D模型赶鸭子上架我也能理解，但是我寻思就不能加点战损大破啥的2D演出吗...... 总体来说，值得一玩的游戏，但是如果把立绘发pixiv的话对我个人来说连玩的必要也没有了，横向对比吸血鬼like的几个同类型选手，人家还有踩踩背和一系列个人剧情呢，还是希望作者能够抓住自己的优势区间，也希望作者能够进一步完善游戏内容，起码底子还是到及格线上的。 我还是想说，真玩力竭了哥 又玩了几个小时，拿到奶牛之后局内体验好了很多，但是bug实在太多了，游戏内容也全是在角色和建筑上面，地图就这么四张，头二十个小时玩完就是纯粹的刷刷刷和挂机，实在是玩不下去了……制作组还是听劝的，但是也没那么听劝，还是期待一下后续的更新或者新作品吧

《禁忌星域》是一款融合了Roguelite采集生存射击与机甲养成的科幻背景题材的类幸存者游戏，只不过游戏以美少女和擦边内容为额外噱头。但是其较为糟糕的建模和视觉效果导致游戏的整体体验打了折扣。 [h1]挖矿与生存的类幸存者玩法[/h1] 本作游戏的核心玩法就是类幸存者的生存玩法，玩家需要在不断涌来的敌人之中存活下去，并获得成长。同时游戏给我的体验也像是《深岩银河幸存者》，在生存战斗的同时，玩家也可以前往地图上的各个点，接触点位和附近的物体进行挖矿采集，收集其中的金币、经验。这样的设定之下，即便玩家不积极进行战斗也可以获得所需的金钱和经验用来提升等级，让机甲成长。 游戏中的战斗以自动的形式，玩家接近敌人就可以使用手中的近战武器和枪械自动对敌人进行攻击。近战武器有使用CD时间，而枪械类武器打完弹药之后也需要一段时间的换弹时间。 当角色的等级提升，玩家可以在随机出现的三个升级项中进行选择提升能力。达到一定等级之后还可以解锁全新的装备武器，让多种武器一齐攻击可以获得更高的火力和更高的攻击效率。随着玩家完成的阶段增长，敌人的难度也越来越高，玩家需要及时跟上自身的能力，才能在接下来的冒险中继续生存。 [h1]美少女元素与擦边内容[/h1] 本作游戏的玩法与深岩银河如此接近，只是各方面建模、手感等都相对薄弱一些。但是游戏却使用了各种美少女元素来改变其根本的观感和体验，吸引了大量的LSP游玩。而游戏中更是不吝使用各种擦边的内容，包括不限于果体内容和百合元素等，对于游戏的内容方面进行了大胆的设计。 [h1]收集资源建设基地的局外成长[/h1] 本作游戏依然存在局外成长的元素，不断加强主角方的实力。玩家在局内通过收集各种资源，其中也有可以带出局外的建造资源，用来建设建造基地，升级科技树，解锁各种新内容等。局外成长增加了游戏后面的可玩性，也降低了战斗难度，是肉鸽类游戏中非常必要的内容，也延长了游戏的寿命。 [table][td][b]欢迎关注我们 [/b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/10591434/]突突突发糖辣！[/url] [/td][/table]

A lust themed survivors shooter that mixes resource-focused runs, evolving weapons and mechs, base building, offline progression, and risqué visuals into a grind heavy but content rich experience. Once again, humanity turns its attention toward space exploration, driven by its endless hunger for wealth and resources. Time and time again, the promise of distant planets has justified dangerous expeditions into the unknown. This journey begins no differently, until one particular mission uncovers something wholly unexpected. The crew discovers a planet ruled by a god. Unlike the familiar archetypes of cruel deities associated with death, war, or greed, this god embodies raw, overwhelming lust. Its presence alone causes the crew aboard the spaceship to sweat uncontrollably, their minds clouded by desire and an intense urge to undress. Before they can exploit the planet or even escape it, they must confront and defeat this god without surrendering to their own impulses. As is typical for the genre, you begin the game with access to only one playable character. Additional characters must be unlocked using currency earned by clearing stages. Each character has three unique perks that improve as you continue to play with them. However, characters are only one part of the equation; your choice of mech is more important because each comes with a unique weapon. After choosing a character and mech, you select one of four worlds that must be played in order. The core gameplay will feel familiar to anyone who has played a survivors style game. You move freely across the map while your weapons fire automatically at nearby enemies. Reloading is also automatic but slow, so you’re forced to keep moving. Surviving for a set amount of time is the main objective, but you also need gather resources scattered across the map. These resources appear as blocks or stations. To extract them, you must stand nearby and break them down. Blocks collapse quickly and reward you almost instantly, while stations require you to remain close for a longer period before releasing their contents. Outside of resource gathering, the fundamentals remain familiar. Enemies drop experience orbs when defeated, and collecting these is essential for leveling up. Experience can also be obtained from special blocks placed around the map, allowing you to grow stronger even when dense enemy swarms block access to dropped orbs. When your experience bar fills, you level up and are presented with three randomly selected upgrades or modules. These fall into several categories. The first is the enhancement module, which improves your weapon’s core statistics. These include increased damage, faster attack speed, larger magazine size, and similar. Occasionally, upgrades appear at a higher rarity, marked by a different color and offering significantly stronger effects. For example, a standard magazine upgrade may increase capacity by twenty percent, while a higher rarity version boosts it by forty percent. Choosing these stronger upgrades is a smart idea. The second category is the general module. Unlike enhancement modules, these upgrades affect your character rather than your weapons. Options include increased movement speed, higher critical hit chance, additional health, and other fundamental bonuses. Next are evolution modules, which add powerful perks to your weapons. Some evolution modules combine multiple stat increases into one upgrade, offering higher percentages than standard enhancements. Others introduce entirely new effects that significantly alter weapon behavior. Examples include firing a circular burst of bullets whenever you reload or causing missiles to leave burning zones on the ground. The rarest upgrades are overlocking modules. These can only be obtained by completing special events marked by chests on the map. To unlock them, you must clear all surrounding blocks and then stand within a marked area until a progress circle fills. While overlocking perks may not seem impressive at first glance, they often provide subtle but meaningful improvements that become increasingly valuable over longer runs. Weapons are a bit different story. Every seventh level up replaces the usual upgrades with new weapons. You can select only one weapon, but additional weapons can be equipped after the next seventh level. Each weapon includes a brief description and four core statistics, such as damage and reload time, allowing for quick evaluation. If none of the options appeal to you, a limited reroll system lets you refresh the selection, a feature that also applies to modules. Until you unlock your second weapon, all upgrades focus solely on your starting weapon, allowing you to strengthen it significantly. While adding new weapons increases the chance of receiving upgrades you may not want, weapon variety remains important. Once a weapon has been upgraded eight times, the next upgrade transforms it into a superior version with dramatically improved statistics. Enemies spawn continuously, appearing at a safe distance to prevent unfair damage. Basic enemies fall quickly, while elite units appear periodically and require more effort to defeat. These tougher enemies drop better loot, including bonuses that allow you to select multiple perks in succession. Each planet is divided into several stages, each ending with a boss fight. A progress bar at the top of the screen signals the boss’s arrival. Defeating the boss quickly is encouraged, as prolonged fights cause regular enemies to grow stronger over time. If the battle drags on, you risk being overwhelmed. Defeating the boss opens a shop where you can spend coins dropped by enemies on additional modules before moving on to the next stage, which introduces more dangerous enemies and harsher environments. Failure is common, but it feeds into the game’s long term progression through its base building system. You manage two main stations: a planetary outpost and an orbital command center, both with several structures. Buildings are predetermined, removing strategic complexity, and only require resources to construct. Resources are generated automatically over time, with the option to manually collect more for faster gains. Each structure has a storage limit, preventing infinite accumulation, but upgrades increase both storage capacity and production speed. Importantly, resource generation continues even when the game is not running, allowing you to collect rewards when you return. These resources are spent on permanent upgrades divided into three categories. Talents provide straightforward bonuses such as increased armor, automatic healing, and bonus experience. They are split into survival, damage, and support trees, each requiring different materials. Support talents are especially valuable but demand rarer resources. Technology upgrades unlock new buildings and improve efficiency, while mech construction allows you to build eleven additional mechs, each requiring a substantial investment. Visually, the game leans heavily into provocative design. Characters are voluptuous women in revealing outfits and suggestive poses. While there is no explicit nudity, the presentation pushes boundaries. One mechanic in particular may raise eyebrows. Characters have a sanity meter that must be restored after several missions, tied to a mini game featuring exaggerated animations and suggestive sounds. Fortunately, an option exists to skip this entirely. Overall, the game delivers strong gameplay, extensive content, and a satisfying progression loop. Its risqué presentation may not appeal to everyone, but it does not detract from the mechanics. With its blend of active runs and passive resource generation, it accommodates both long sessions and brief check ins, making it accessible despite its grind heavy structure.

I bought this looking for a Vampire Survivors clone that had a sci-fi/mecha angle and I'm pretty satisfied overall. I'm a huge fan of mecha musume, so having the characters be big-chested cyborg women was a huge plus. Overall, the game satisfies my expectations and adds some nice variation to the genre. First, the maps contain mining spots where you can stand to crack open hexagonal cylinders that give you resources: either XP or currency. The game has a VERY gacha style layout with tons of different currencies that are used to purchase higher tiers of skills, unlock new resources and so forth. Thankfully, the game isn't actually monetized like a mobile gacha - it just resembles it stylistically. In any case, the mining aspect is actually a nice QOL addition since some starting weapons are weaker than others early on. So being able to mine XP to get better weapon tiers helps balance the weapon choices. Very smart addition. Second, progress in the game is gated not only behind unlocking things through achievements but also building resource-generating structures. The resource management mini-game is nowhere near as complex as something like Factorio. I suppose it is more like the factory system in Arknights Endfield, wherein you build structures and those structures produce...things that can be spent on other things and so forth. It's actually kind of satisfying seeing "number go up" and then blowing like 30K on an unlock. Actual gameplay is identical to other casual, VS-clones: you move your character around a map whilst waves of enemies are generated and thrown at you and you kill them and get XP. After a certain period of time, a boss is spawned and killing it ends the run. However, rather than having you spend ~30 minutes on the same level, maps are randomly generated each time and split into ~4 minute periods. In between the periods, you are given a shop menu where you can buy the same kinds of upgrades you get from consuming XP (again helping balance and progression). Overall, it's a nice change of pace from other VS-likes that often are quite demanding of your time. In fact, this game encourages you to take breaks since the resource minigame continues even when the game is off and gives you bonus acquisition if you leave it off for 6+ hours. There are only a few criticisms I can give. First, the game's frame rate will often stutter as it attempts to spawn in certain waves of enemies or items on the field. It's not game-breaking but it is a little annoying and I don't think it is anything that can be fixed by changing the settings. Some enemies or items are just more resource-intensive and the code just doesn't handle it well. But, again, these are very brief stutters. The game will run smoothly 99.9% of the time. The only other issue (as of this writing) is, being a translated game, the translation is extremely poor with bad grammar and very confusing sentences all over. It took me a few hours of playing to fully realize what some of the instructions and menus were actually telling me. I still don't really understand what a "void purification effect" actually is. Fortunately, being a VS-like, the game is simple enough that none of that really matters. It has the same basic expectations as other VS-likes so you're probably not going to get too confused. I will say that the formatting of the translation is also extremely poor. Words will overlap each other and not fit in the boxes and sometimes become very hard to physically read. But it does look like the devs are keeping up with the game and this is something that is a very easy fix if they either co-opt a native English speaker or just spend a little more time formatting. Finally, there is a slight ecchi component to the game but it's rather mild. Every time you sortie with the girls, they lose "sanity." If sanity reaches zero, you can still use them but they take more damage and get some other maluses. To restore their sanity, you have to play a "massage" style mini-game where you roll the scroll button on your mouse (I don't know what happens if you don't have a scroll button but it's 2026 and if your mouse doesn't have one consider getting a real job and buying one). The girls will make quite loud moaning sounds as you play the mini-game and their clothes come off for some reason. There's no full-frontal nudity though. Mercifully, you can skip the mini-game if you level up an associated building enough. I immediately opted to do that since it's incredibly frustrating having to spend 1-2 minutes helping them flick their bean after every mission. Overall, the ecchi component is extremely awful and not worth it if you are interested in the game for that reason. The character designs are nice and interesting though. And they do "react" if you click on them (although I will say the live2d animations are...not amazing). Overall, I'm pretty happy with the game and it is at the right price point. I'd highly recommend it if you want a VS-clone with a different coat of paint and like mecha girls.

It's either a mobile game port or designed as a mobile game initially & pivoted mid-development. After 9 hours of playing I still don't understand how to unlock the rest of the characters (I only unlocked two, not including the first) and have barely been able to touch any of the elements to make my character(s) or weapons stronger. Base building is tedious, resources are irritating to acquire in-game. In-match progression doesn't make any sense, and isn't explained (I assumed it's like Vampire Survivors but the forums seem to suggest otherwise??) Matches are not seamless. You fight a boss and then are forcibly moved to a "new" section of the map with altered harvestable locations. You need an absurd amount of one type of resource to upgrade the resource generating towers outside of matches (that continue counting while the game is offline) and you can only get a lot of them from one map. The power-based progression is tied to a menu that has broken English, and 90% of the nodes don't make any sense or have no explanation at all. Controls with a controller are not intuitive in menus (the d-pad and analogue stick do different things.) There's so many things wrong with this game that seems like there's nobody doing any kind of QoL passes. I spend all the time I play in the same mission, farming the same resources with no real incentive to play the other maps. Even if I did, the enemy variety is lacking, there's a bunch of projectiles from them that do nothing, the build variety is poor and evolving weapons is unclear and can even break your build (a sniper weapon build with one massive damage bullet can be combined with a rapid firing AR, and when evolved it makes a weapon that's supposed to be fired extremely quickly but only has one bullet.) For me to recommend this game it needs the following: Complete revamp of base resource requirements Complete revamp of in-match resource collection Clear explanations of unlocking characters Fixing all broken English and formatting Better explanations in English Seamless missions Fixing & streamlining controller function in menus Even on sale I don't recommend this game in it's current state. It's unlikely to change.

Overall an enjoyable game, but with a bunch of minor issues. It has all the bells and whistles of a survivor-like game. Different characters, a ton of weapons, weapon evolutions, meta-progressions, etc. Some of things it did right: 1. indication of affected weapons before you commit to picking a buff 2. a large variety of evolution module (or weapon perks), Each weapon allows you to pick 2 of 4 different unique perks and these perks (+ fusion perk) can be inherited to its fusion version; fusion weapon also has a list of unique perks that you can choose 2 from. 2. you have the choice of fusion weapon or keeping it in its base form (called mutation, usually it provide a sort of buff to your build), 3. real time damage split so you can optimize survival by picking buffs that affect your damage the most However if there is a non-cumulative damage (something like DPS for last minute of playtime) would even be better 4. serviceable co-op. Requires a lot of polishing but it's working and you can play with friends (up to 4). I have only tried playing with 1 other friend so I cannot tell what type of chaos 4 players would have. However there are also things that could be improved, and these are the opinion of someone who beat endless mode 50+ getting the last gameplay related achievement 1. Evolution doesn't keep your original weapon type: what i mean is, you can start with a weapon with [Light][Charge][Element][Radiation][Range][Flame] and most of the possible evolution would make you lose 1 or more of these tags for a different tag. 2. Follow-up of 1. mutation (keeping a weapon at its base form after level 9) is an option, but it's a bad one because the stat provided usually aren't significant enough as is, let along that some of these global passive provided doesn't even work in late game. Some example: sniper rifle firing a round after other weapon reload, or shotgun buffing the rest of your weapon while it's reloading but a yellow buff "Lucky Reload" basically remove reloading entirely. The dev could consider changing mutation passive to fix this. 3. Sloppy translation: Evil-dispelling is exorcism, and the term get used interchangeably, this can get a bit confusing. There are some buff that affect Defense type weapon, but no weapon is labeled as Defense type, however some of the weapons are designated as Defense type, such as the shotgun and the grenade. 4. Really just lack of information from within the game. You can research Mechs in the game, and they change what your starting weapon is. These Mechs have different tiers and researching them cost different amount of different materials. However the difference between T1 and T2 and T3 are not very clearly stated in game. The higher tiers allow you to use better randomized starting buffs, but beyond that? Unclear. 5. Coomer aesthetic and even story BUT nothing beyond surface level. 6. Game is frankly unoptimized at the endgame. Literally slideshow at the end. Glad to see the game getting updated. Rating changed to reflect my optimism.
